sections.title: The letter cé
paragraphs: The name of this letter is (cé) /se/. Its main sound is heard in the word (café) /ka.fe/, which means coffee. This letter makes two different spoken sounds, and sometimes it makes no sound at all.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: For the first sound, push the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Stop the air, then release it sharply with no puff of air. For the second sound, put your tongue tip near the ridge behind your upper teeth. Push the air out through the narrow gap. Keep your throat quiet for both sounds.

sections.title: Spelling patterns
paragraphs: This letter makes the sound in (carte) /kaʁt/ before the letters a, o or u, and before consonants. It makes the hissing sound in (cerise) /sə.ʁiz/ before e, i or y. A special mark under the letter also gives that hissing sound before a, o or u, as in (garçon) /gaʁ.sɔ̃/. At the end of some words, it is a silent letter, as in (tabac) /ta.ba/ and (porc) /pɔʁ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not blow a puff of air when you make the first sound. It is not like the plosive in English cat. A plosive is a consonant where the air stops for a moment and then bursts out. Hold the air tightly and keep it clean. Do not pronounce the final letter in words where it stays quiet.
